items: The OOP concept that hides data inside a class is: (a) Inheritance (b) Polymorphism (c) Encapsulation (d) Abstraction

Classes and objects in Object-Oriented Programming are best described as: (a) Classes are real-world entities, and objects are methods. (b) Classes are blueprints, and objects are instances of those blueprints. (c) Classes are used for data storage, and objects are used for functionality. (d) Objects define functionality, and classes store data.

The main idea behind encapsulation in OOP is: (a) To hide data inside a class and prevent unauthorised access. (b) To create a flexible and adaptable programme. (c) To reuse code from other classes. (d) To allow multiple inheritance in classes.

Inheritance in OOP means: (a) Reusing and extending functionality from a parent class to a child class. (b) Hiding data in a class. (c) Creating multiple instances of the same class. (d) Managing polymorphic behaviour of classes.

Polymorphism in OOP is best defined as: (a) Allowing an object to take multiple forms through method overriding. (b) Hiding data inside a class for security. (c) Using multiple inheritance to extend classes. (d) Ensuring that each object has only one method.

An example of inheritance in Python is: (a) Creating two classes with similar attributes. (b) A child class inheriting attributes and methods from a parent class. (c) Using private variables within a class. (d) Modifying a method inside the same class.

The purpose of polymorphism in programming is: (a) To create reusable functions with multiple parameter types. (b) To allow a function or method to have different implementations. (c) To combine different classes into a single class. (d) To manage the flow of control in a programme.
The keyword used to define a class in Python is: (a) def (b) class (c) function (d) object

Encapsulation is best described as: (a) Combining data and methods into a single unit and controlling access to data. (b) Combining multiple classes into one class. (c) Inheriting methods from other classes. (d) Allowing objects to have multiple forms.
Inheritance allows a class to: (a) Hide its data only. (b) Inherit attributes and methods from another class. (c) Define multiple functions only. (d) Create objects without a class.
